idiom_name: two-case value (success | failure) with a short-circuiting bind and a terminal handler
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: define one type with exactly two constructors - the success payload and the failure reason - and make those constructors the only way to build a result, so a failure can never be mistaken for data. Provide one composition step (bind/and_then, spelled ? or for/yield where the language offers it) that applies the next fallible operation only when the current value is a success and otherwise returns the existing failure unchanged; keep mapping helpers for adapting either payload and an accumulating combinator for the cases where every failure must be reported. Consume the result exactly once, exhaustively, in a terminal handler that chooses the policy - default, translate, retry, propagate - and let a must-use check or a lint rule make a dropped result visible. Convert exceptions, sentinel codes and null at the boundary where they originate, and keep the failure payload a structured value (code, enum, variant), never a formatted message.
code_sketch:
step: input -> Result<value, error>            # each step owns one failure kind
parse(input).and_then(validate).and_then(store) # first Failure bypasses the rest
            .map(render_id)
match result:                                  # terminal handler, both cases
    Success(value) -> use(value)
    Failure(error) -> handle(error)            # default | translate | retry | propagate
pitfalls: Encoding failure as a sentinel of the payload type (0, -1, empty string) defeats the two constructors and reintroduces in-band signalling.
Leaving the result un-consumed or immediately unwrapped turns the pattern into decoration: the failure still crashes or disappears, one frame later.
Growing one global error enum for every layer makes the failure value meaningless; keep an error type per boundary and translate between them.

Wrong move: replace every exception, including invariant bugs and infrastructure faults, with Result -> diagnostics and recovery policy collapse into an opaque union -> instead model expected domain failures and keep exceptions or panics for unrecoverable faults.

Wrong move: use fail-fast bind for field validation -> the first error hides independent invalid fields -> instead switch deliberately to an accumulating validation or applicative form when callers need every diagnostic.

Wrong move: unwrap or getOrThrow immediately after every Result -> failure still aborts one frame later while the signature adds ceremony -> instead propagate with bind or ? and handle both cases at the terminal boundary.
